title: Websites & E-commerce
subtitle: Give your brand a home online: a landing page and a small store, built with Claude (artifacts and Claude Code) and put online with Vercel. Learn page parts, words that sell, vibe coding, checkout, trust and user testing.
bigIdea: A website is a set of files a browser draws on the screen. A great landing page has one goal and tells a story from top to bottom, ending in one clear button. AI can write the code, but you are the boss: you plan it, check it, test it with real people and make sure it's honest and works for everyone.
objectives: Explain how a web page reaches your screen, and what HTML, CSS and JavaScript do.
Plan a landing page with 6 parts and a phone-first wireframe.
Write clear, honest copy: headlines, benefits and button words.
Build a real website with Claude Code, put it online with Vercel, and vibe-code a custom section with Claude.
Open a small store with honest product cards, fair prices and a safe checkout (order form or test payment link).
Make the site work for everyone and trustworthy, then improve it with real user tests.

vocabulary.definition: A set of pages anyone can open on the internet.
vocabulary.analogy: A shop window that never closes.
vocabulary.example: sipsquad.example

vocabulary.definition: The name you type to find a page.
vocabulary.analogy: A street address for a house.
vocabulary.example: https://sipsquad-site.vercel.app

vocabulary.definition: The 3 kinds of web code: what's on the page, how it looks, what happens when you click.
vocabulary.analogy: A house's rooms, its paint, and its lights.
vocabulary.example: A button (HTML) that's teal (CSS) and opens a pop-up (JavaScript).

vocabulary.definition: A computer that keeps your site online so others can see it.
vocabulary.analogy: Renting a spot in a mall for your shop.
vocabulary.example: Vercel hosts your site for free and updates it every time you save a change.

vocabulary.definition: Claude's live preview of something it built, right next to the chat. You can publish it with a link.
vocabulary.analogy: A sketch you can already click on.
vocabulary.example: A one-page site you made in your first lesson.

vocabulary.definition: Claude working as a coder: it makes and changes all the files of a project for you.
vocabulary.analogy: A builder who follows your plans and shows you every change.
vocabulary.example: 'Add a Shop page with 3 product cards.'

vocabulary.definition: A repo is a project's folder on GitHub that remembers every change. Deploy means putting it online.
vocabulary.analogy: A notebook with every draft saved, and a printer that publishes the newest page.
vocabulary.example: Claude Code saves to the repo; Vercel deploys the site.

vocabulary.definition: One page made for one goal, like 'buy this'.
vocabulary.analogy: A movie poster: one film, one message.
vocabulary.example: A page for the Sip Bottle with one 'Order now' button.

vocabulary.definition: The big top part of a page that people see first.
vocabulary.analogy: The front cover of a book.
vocabulary.example: A headline, one line, a picture and a button.

vocabulary.definition: A simple box sketch of a page, before colors and pictures.
vocabulary.analogy: A floor plan before building a house.
vocabulary.example: Boxes for hero, reasons, proof and footer on a phone shape.

vocabulary.definition: The words on a website or ad.
vocabulary.analogy: The script for a play.
vocabulary.example: 'Water bottles that never leak.'

vocabulary.definition: A feature is a fact about the product. A benefit is what it does for you.
vocabulary.analogy: 'Big engine' vs. 'gets you there fast'.
vocabulary.example: 'Double steel walls' → 'ice-cold water for 24 hours'.

vocabulary.definition: Building software by describing what you want to an AI, then testing and fixing it.
vocabulary.analogy: Being the director while the AI is the film crew.
vocabulary.example: Asking Claude for a 'Which bottle is for you?' quiz, then testing and fixing it.

vocabulary.definition: A clear note about a mistake: what I did, what should happen, what really happened.
vocabulary.analogy: Telling a doctor exactly where it hurts.
vocabulary.example: 'I clicked Next on question 3. My result should show. Nothing happened.'

vocabulary.definition: A short description of a picture, read out loud by screen readers.
vocabulary.analogy: A friend describing a photo to you on the phone.
vocabulary.example: 'Teal water bottle with ice on a mossy rock.'

vocabulary.definition: A box for one product: picture, name, price, short words and a button.
vocabulary.analogy: A price tag with a sales pitch.
vocabulary.example: Sip Bottle, Teal, $20, 'Add to cart'.

vocabulary.definition: The steps to buy something online.
vocabulary.analogy: The line at the store's register.
vocabulary.example: Cart → Details → Pay → Thank you.

vocabulary.definition: A practice mode for payments with pretend money and pretend cards.
vocabulary.analogy: Playing a store with toy money.
vocabulary.example: A Stripe Payment Link in test mode.

vocabulary.definition: A sneaky design that tricks people into buying or signing up.
vocabulary.analogy: A shop that hides the exit.
vocabulary.example: A fake 'only 2 left!' timer.

vocabulary.definition: Watching a real person try to use your site, without helping.
vocabulary.analogy: A taste test for a new recipe.
vocabulary.example: 'Please order a teal bottle and think out loud.'

vocabulary.definition: A saved change in your repo, with a short note about what changed.
vocabulary.analogy: A save point in a video game.
vocabulary.example: "Add the hero section"

tools.name: Claude (artifacts)
tools.bestFor: MAIN TOOL: writing copy, quick one-page sites and trying custom sections (quizzes, calculators) as live previews you can publish with a link
tools.freeTier: Free plan can make and publish artifacts; paid plans give more use
tools.minAge: 18+ for Claude accounts. College students: use your own account.
tools.classroomUse: Lessons 1, 3, 5 and every lesson where Claude helps with words, checks or fixes.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.bestFor: MAIN BUILDER for the real website: makes and changes every file in the site's GitHub repo, adds pages, the shop and fixes
tools.freeTier: Needs a paid Claude plan (Pro or higher). Works on the web (claude.ai/code) and in the Claude desktop app.
tools.classroomUse: From lesson 4 on: build, add the custom section, shop, privacy page and fixes.
tools.alternative: Publish the site as a Claude artifact link

tools.name: GitHub + Vercel
tools.bestFor: Storing the site's files (GitHub) and putting it online with a real web address that updates on every save (Vercel)
tools.minAge: GitHub 13+, Vercel 18+ for the account owner
tools.classroomUse: Lesson 4 sets them up once; every later change deploys by itself.

tools.name: Google Forms + Sheets
tools.bestFor: Order forms, feedback surveys and a pricing sheet
tools.alternative: A Claude-built form section (later, with a real backend)

tools.name: Stripe Payment Links (test mode)
tools.bestFor: Practicing a real online checkout with pretend cards
tools.freeTier: Free to set up. Test mode costs nothing. Real payments have fees.
tools.classroomUse: Optional level-up in lesson 8. Stay in test mode in class.

tools.name: Screen readers (TalkBack, VoiceOver, ChromeVox)
tools.bestFor: Testing your site the way blind and low-vision visitors use it
tools.freeTier: Free, built into phones and computers
tools.classroomUse: Lesson 6 warm-up and Screen Reader Race.

tools.name: Gemini (pictures)
tools.bestFor: Product pictures, icons and banners in your brand style (your picture tool from Module 1)
tools.classroomUse: Lessons 4 and 7 for any new pictures.

toolsVerified: November 2026 (Claude artifact publishing and Claude Code access checked). Set up for college students (18+), so all tools are open. Claude is the main builder for websites, agents, apps and games.

gamification.questLine: Your launch video is ready. Now your company needs a home online: a landing page where people learn about it and a small store where they can order.
gamification.badge: 🌐 Web Smith: a live landing page + store that scores 3 or more on every rubric row.
gamification.boss: Launch Day: a live walkthrough from the hero to a test order, with guests as 'first customers'. 1-on-1: launch for the teacher plus a guest.
sideQuests: Under the hood: read the code of your custom Claude section and explain 5 lines of the code in your own words (+25 XP).
Dark Pattern Detective: find a real store with a sneaky design and write a polite note on how to fix it (+25 XP).
A/B test: run two headlines with different testers and report which one won and why (+25 XP).
Custom domain: connect a real web address to your site on Vercel (+25 XP).

safety.teach: Collect only what you need (name, email, product, address if shipping). Never ask for card numbers in a form. Keep the order sheet private and delete it when done.
Stay in Stripe test mode in class. Real money brings real rules (fees, taxes, refunds). If a student wants to sell for real, they should check local rules first.
No dark patterns: no fake timers, hidden fees, pre-ticked boxes or fake reviews. Pictures, prices and promises must match what the buyer gets. Label AI pictures.
Strong passwords and 2-step verification on Claude, GitHub, Vercel, Google and Stripe. Learn to spot phishing messages and fake stores.
A deployed site or published artifact can be seen by anyone. Use a brand email; never post a home address or personal phone number, and never put passwords or keys in the repo.
Alt text, contrast, headings, clear link words and captions, so people with disabilities can use the site too.

finalProject.title: Live Landing Page + Mini Store
finalProject.brief: Use the made-up company, Brand Kit and launch video from Modules 1 and 2. Plan, write and build a landing page and a small store with Claude Code, put it online with Vercel, add one custom section vibe-coded with Claude and a working checkout (order form or Stripe test payment link). Test it with real people, fix it, then launch it live. In a group, launch to the class. 1-on-1, launch to the teacher and a guest.
deliverables: Live site on Vercel (built with Claude Code): landing page with launch video, Shop page with 3+ product cards, Privacy & Rules page
One custom section vibe-coded with Claude, live and working, with 2+ bug reports in the Prompt Log
Working checkout: order form or Stripe test payment link, with a thank-you message
User test notes from 2+ people and a fix list with the top 3 fixes done
Works for Everyone and Trust checklists passed

levels: No clear goal or page parts missing
Most parts there, but the goal is fuzzy
One clear goal, all 6 parts, hero clear in 5 seconds
Every section moves the visitor toward the goal, and choices are explained with web words
Site not published, or broken parts
Clean on phones and computers, brand theme, working custom section
Custom section fits the brand and helps buyers decide; clear bug reports show the fix process
No store or no way to order
Products listed, but prices or checkout unclear
3+ honest product cards, fair prices, working checkout with thank-you message
Smooth, fast checkout that asks only for what's needed, with clear shipping and returns
Tricks, missing privacy info or no alt text
Both checklists pass; tested with 2+ people and top fixes made
Explains what testing changed, how the store protects buyers' data, and who the access fixes help

finalProject.levelUp: Connect a custom web address, add an email sign-up with a Claude-written welcome email, and make a 9:16 version of the launch video for social posts that link to the store.

support: Web Prompt Recipe card and a ready example prompt to copy.
Wireframe sheet with the 6 boxes already drawn.
Copy frames: '[Product] that [benefit], so you can [feeling].'
A starter build prompt with blanks to fill; the one-page artifact link is fine as a first version.
Group: Builder and Tester roles, swapping each lesson. 1-on-1: the student builds and you test, then swap for the custom section.
extension: Add a second page (FAQ or About) with a menu.
Make the quiz result link straight to the matching product.
Run a WAVE accessibility check and fix the top 3 issues.
Try a Stripe test Payment Link with options and a redirect back to the site.

carryForward: The store's orders, emails and questions become the 'busy work' that students automate with AI helpers in Module 4 (Agents & Workflows).
